parts.name: Oesophagus (lower end)
parts.info: The muscular food pipe. Waves of contraction push food down into the stomach.
parts.fact: A ring of muscle at its lower end stops acid from washing back up; when it fails, you get heartburn.

parts.name: Cardia
parts.info: The area just around the opening from the oesophagus.
parts.fact: Its name comes from being the part of the stomach closest to the heart.

parts.name: Fundus
parts.info: The dome rising above the entry of the oesophagus. It often holds swallowed air.
parts.fact: On an X-ray taken standing up, the gas bubble in the fundus is easy to see.

parts.name: Body of the stomach
parts.info: The large central part where food is mixed with acid and enzymes.
parts.fact: Glands here make the hydrochloric acid and pepsin that start protein digestion.

parts.name: Pyloric antrum
parts.info: The lower part that grinds food into a soupy mix called chyme.
parts.fact: Strong muscle waves here squirt small amounts of chyme onward and push the rest back to mix again.

parts.name: Pylorus
parts.info: A thick ring of muscle that controls the flow of chyme into the duodenum.
parts.fact: In some babies this muscle overgrows and blocks the stomach outlet, causing forceful vomiting.

parts.name: Duodenum
parts.info: The C-shaped first part of the small intestine, where bile and pancreatic juice join the food.
parts.fact: It is about 25 cm long, roughly the width of twelve fingers, which is what its Latin name means.

parts.name: Mucosa (inner lining)
parts.info: The soft inner lining. In the stomach it lies in folds called rugae that flatten out as the stomach fills.
parts.fact: The stomach lining replaces itself every few days so the acid doesn't digest it.
